instruction:
GUI-only requirement: Complete the entire task through the launched graphical user interfaces only. Do not open Terminal, Command Prompt, PowerShell, or any shell. Do not run Python, VBA, macros, Abaqus noGUI, ANSYS command scripts, batch/headless tools, APIs, or helper code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only the native AutoCAD, SolidWorks, and Abaqus/CAE GUI tools, menus, dialogs, editors, and built-in import, export, save, submit, and solve commands.

Three-software CAE flow: AutoCAD -> SolidWorks -> Abaqus/CAE. No init files are provided; start from blank files.

Chain evidence requirement: use the design token EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_05. In AutoCAD, add a readable label containing EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_05 and AUTOCAD_TO_SOLIDWORKS on a CHAIN layer in stage1_profile.dxf. In SolidWorks, keep EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_05, FROM_stage1_profile.dxf, and SOLIDWORKS_TO_ABAQUS encoded in the part/custom properties or STEP export metadata so the text of stage2_geometry.step contains them. In Abaqus/CAE, create at least one model, part, instance, set, surface, job description, or other native name containing both EW_ACAD_SW_ABQ_05 and IMPORTED_FROM_stage2_geometry.step, so the final CAE file carries evidence that Abaqus consumed the SolidWorks STEP handoff.


1. In AutoCAD, use GUI drawing tools only to create the 2D profile and save it as C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_profile.dxf. Draw a 180 mm x 70 mm thin-plate outline on layer OUTLINE, two longitudinal bead centerlines on layer REFERENCE, and end loading edge markers.
2. In SolidWorks, import stage1_profile.dxf through the GUI, create a 2 mm thick plate with two 3 mm high longitudinal ribs, and export C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage2_geometry.step.
3. In Abaqus/CAE, import stage2_geometry.step through the GUI and create the finite-element model. Use the model name Model-RibPlateBuckle. Define material Steel with E=210000 MPa and nu=0.3, create a section using Steel, and assign it to the ribbed plate. Create a shell idealization of the thin ribbed plate from the imported geometry and mesh it with coarse S4R shell elements; avoid a dense 3D solid tetrahedral mesh. Create a linear buckle step named Step-Buckle requesting 5 eigenvalues. Create sets named FIXED_EDGE and LOAD_EDGE. Create a boundary condition named BC-FixedEdge that constrains FIXED_EDGE. Create a load named Load-Compression400N that applies an approximately 400 N compressive edge load at LOAD_EDGE. Submit the job named Job-RibPlateBuckle and wait for the analysis to complete.
4. Required deliverables on the Desktop: C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_profile.dxf, C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage2_geometry.step, C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-RibPlateBuckle.cae, and C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-RibPlateBuckle.odb. Do not create extra STEP, DXF, CAE, or ODB deliverables.

[Software] Open and use AutoCAD, SolidWorks, and Abaqus/CAE one at a time through the Windows GUI as needed. First use AutoCAD to create the DXF profile, then use SolidWorks to import the DXF and export the STEP file, then use Abaqus/CAE to import that STEP file, build the finite-element model, submit the job, and save the CAE and ODB deliverables.
